rules.sentence: Diskitis is a serious but uncommon medical diagnosis.

Treatment consists of a prolonged antibiotic course, but usually results in uncomplicated resolution of symptoms; however, delay in treatment or misdiagnosis can lead to significant morbidity and mortality.
In the majority of cases, diskitis stems from 1 of 3 inciting events: direct inoculation, hematogenous spread, or, less commonly, contiguous spread.[1]
Identification of the causative agent is difficult, if not impossible, at times.[2]
When positive cultures are obtained, the most commonly identified organism is Staphylococcus aureus.[2][3]
Also implicated, although less frequently, are coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Escherichia coli, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Salmonellaspp.[2]
Fungi have also been causative agents.[2]
